title: Finish story-linked ad hoc sessions in the Dashboard

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-432 "Finish story-linked ad hoc sessions" (.planning/seeds/SEED-432-finish-story-linked-ad-hoc-sessions.md#finish-story-linked-ad-hoc-sessions), plan 813 slice 2, revision 03b6dc4abe9f49901a6119f8e2295d04165ef75d.

Promise: An isolated Start that is not a follow-up publishes one canonical story and its Taken assignment before it opens a native session. A refused admission, a competing claim or an origin mismatch opens no native session.

Verdict: Insufficient evidence. The fault did not produce the promised wrong behaviour. A maintained assertion failed, but no native session opened, so the run never exercised the wrong path.

Fault (one edit, fixtures and assertions intact): dashboard/server/isolatedSessionAdmission.ts, in admitIsolatedSession, just before the `if (result.kind === "prepared")` refusal. Inserted:
  if (result.kind !== "accepted") return { kind: "admitted", revision: (await git(project, ["rev-parse", "HEAD"])).trim() };
With this edit the module reports "admitted" without a confirmed `start --admit` publication. That covers the prepared, stopped, conflict and unreadable cases. This is the caller's suggested fault: return admitted before the publication is confirmed. I did not try the origin-mismatch skip, to keep this to one bounded check.

Maintained checks examined (no fixture added):
- dashboard/backend-tests/launches/admitted-session-refusal.spec.ts: origin mismatch refused before any native start
- dashboard/backend-tests/launches/admitted-session-retry.spec.ts: "Continue allocates a new story after a competing claim wins" and "Continue records a previously accepted publication before native startup"
Command, run in a scratch detached worktree at the revision: env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:backend -- 'admitted-session' --workers=1, with OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_BACKEND_PROOF_RECORD set so each run's reach is recorded. The E2E spec was not run, because of machine load and the one-check bound.

Observations:
- Baseline: exit 0. The proof record shows phase completed, 3 selected, all 3 passed (refusal 663 ms, competing claim 6171 ms, accepted publication 2495 ms).
- Faulted: exit 1. Only the competing-claim test reaches the faulted branch, because there the losing `start --admit` returns stopped/conflict. It failed at admitted-session-retry.spec.ts:119 (`toMatchObject` on the first launch response). The expected explanation contained "Taken by another agent". The received one was {kind: "failed", reason: "start-refused", explanation: "Story admission could not be read. Continue to recover it. ..."}. The other two tests passed. The origin test returns before the faulted line. The accepted-publication test takes the accepted branch.
- Independent check of wrong behaviour: no native session opened. The response stayed kind "failed", not "launched". The reason is a second guard downstream in dashboard/server/unattachedStart.ts (~line 186). When admitsIsolatedStory is true and the kept session start has no claim.publishedSha, it stops with "Story admission could not be read. Continue to recover it." and publication {kind: "unknown"}. So the promise still held under this fault; only the refusal's wording changed. The maintained assertion caught a wording change, not a native session opened without publication.
- Restoration: a shell trap ran `git checkout` on the file. git diff was empty, and the only pre-existing untracked item was my node_modules symlink, which was the pre-probe state. The rerun of the same command exited 0 with phase completed, 3 of 3 passed (1047 / 7470 / 3361 ms). I then removed the scratch worktree and symlink. The execution checkout's tracked files were not touched by this probe. At the end its status showed changes to SEED-413, SEED-432, plan 813 and docs/dashboard-ux-ui-north-star.md that this probe did not make; they look like concurrent wrap-up work.

Next proof action (separate from the verdict): to test whether anything catches a native session opening without publication, the fault has to get past both guards. Either fault the publishedSha guard in unattachedStart.ts together with this one, or plant the fault in that guard. The assertion to watch is `expect(dashboard.claudeLaunchCalls()).toHaveLength(0)` in admitted-session-retry.spec.ts:124. The separate origin-mismatch fault, against admitted-session-refusal.spec.ts, is still untried.

Prior dispositions: none known match this evidence. The probe made no repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, wall-clock seconds from shell timestamps around each backend run): about 13 s baseline, 15 s faulted, 18 s restored, plus one unrecorded discovery run of about 20 s. About 66 s in total.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this delegated run.
- Agent effort: unavailable. This agent has no supported token or turn meter available.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 169427 ms (measured), from 1795600236969 to 1795600406396 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision `03b6dc4abe9f49901a6119f8e2295d04165ef75d`. Verdict: Insufficient evidence, so no delivered defect was found. The downstream kept-start guard in `unattachedStart.ts` held the promise, and the competing-claim assertion still failed on the changed wording. Decision: the next proof action goes into the matching queued work rather than a new correction. [SEED-439](seeds/SEED-439-complete-story-linked-ad-hoc-sessions.md#complete-story-linked-ad-hoc-sessions) plan 833 slice 1 moves default starts onto that guard. There it faults the guard and confirms, or adds, the `claudeLaunchCalls()` zero assertion. The origin-mismatch fault remains untried.
